items.note: The error sits in the black footer. The white email input has a 2px red border, and below it is a small red dot with a short ink message that says what to type. The pink submit button stays next to the field. It follows the reference's error recipe (thick danger border, message in text colour) and keeps the footer's white-input-plus-pink-button form from the reference's subscribe footer.

Same footer error in dark. The input stays white with its red 2px border, as the band and footer rule asks, the dot and message read clearly on black, and the pink 'get the newsletter' block in the header matches the reference's dark CTA turning pink.

On a phone the footer stacks a full-width white input with the red border over a full-width pink button, with the dot and message under the input. That matches the reference's phone footer and stays readable. It is only visible at the bottom of the long page.

The form is replaced by a teal die-cut 'done' word badge, with lemon lettering outlined in ink, beside a two-line thank-you. This closes the earlier 'undesigned success' gap with the spec's word badge. But the badge floats loose on the black footer: there is no white ink panel, and its ink slab disappears into the black.

Identical to light, since the footer is black in both modes. The 'done' badge and message read clearly. As in light, the confirmation has no framed panel, and the slab under the badge can't be seen on black.

The badge sits left of a wrapped three-line message in the phone footer. It is compact and clear, and it is the same loose badge-on-black treatment as on desktop, without the static-shadow white panel the toast and confirmation recipe describes.

The focused search field has a pink focus halo and an ink clear glyph; the blue glyph from the earlier verdict is fixed. Below it is a full-width dashed white box holding a periwinkle magnifier sticker with a lemon handle, a one-line headline, a hint and an outline 'clear' button. This is the reference's dashed empty state, raised with the spec's own-silhouette sticker.

In dark the dashed box becomes a raised grey field with the same magnifier sticker, so the sticker rests on a raised surface as the rule requires. The headline, hint and outline button stay clear. The focus halo on the search field still shows on black.

On a phone the dashed box spans the column. The magnifier sticker stays at about 120px, and the two-line headline, hint and outline button are centred. The filter pills wrap to two lines instead of overflowing, which fixes the earlier cut-off pill row. It is close to the reference's mobile dashed empty state, with more character.

The focused current nav pill (black) gets a 2px ink ring at a 2px offset that follows the pill shape. This matches the reference's focus-visible treatment: a tight ink outline, no glow, no colour change. The hero behind it is unchanged.
In dark the current pill is white with a white ring around it. This matches the reference's dark inversion (white current pill) and stays clearly visible on the black bar.
The 40px menu button gets a doubled ink ring around its hairline box. It is clear and in the drawn-ink language, matching how the reference rings controls.

There are 12 different nouns: a notepad, pencil, envelope, mug and speech bubble in the hero, and a box, ticket, flag, tape, clock, jar and bell on the cards. The card vignettes (the clock, jar and ticket) now have a solid side band. But the hero's largest objects, the notepad and the envelope, still show a side strip only about 4% of their height, so they read as flat outlines with a lip. The mug is about 110px. The reference's coins are thick 200–260px die-cuts with a deep rim.

The article figure is a new three-tile cluster (teal, white, marigold tiles with ink outlines and visible thickness) on periwinkle, and it fits the topic. The related-post vignettes (ticket, tape, flag) are thick and flat-filled in band colours. These are close to the reference's chunky sticker craft at card size.

The figure is two paper sheets with folded corners, one white with a struck line and one marigold with an ink dot, on teal. Each has a solid lower band, and they read as notes. The related vignettes (the box, the tape, the clock) keep the same thick die-cut build.

The single drawing is a marigold clipboard with a white clip and ruled lines on periwinkle. It reads clearly, but its side band is a thin offset sliver, so it looks like a flat card with a shadow edge rather than the reference's heavy die-cut object.

The hero stickers carry only the scroll-linked drift: in the time-based frames the notepad and the mug don't move at all, and they sit at different heights in screenshots taken at different scroll positions. Nothing loops or plays on load. This matches the spec's scroll-bound drift and the reference's restrained, mostly static bands.

findings.summary: Flat paper-like objects (the hero notepad, the hero envelope, the about clipboard) still show a side strip only 3–5% of their height, so the largest stickers on the front page read as flat outlines with a lip. The rounder or boxier objects (the clock, the jar, the ticket, the tape) now carry a proper thick band. The reference's hero objects are uniformly heavy die-cuts with a deep solid rim, and that heft is what makes them weigh against the headline. The earlier sticker-depth gap has closed for some shapes but not for thin, flat nouns.
findings.promptFix: Objects that are thin in real life (a sheet, a pad, an envelope, a card, a clipboard) still get the full sticker thickness. Draw them as a block, as if die-cut from thick board: a pad with a visible page stack, an envelope as a padded mailer. Give the side strip the same 10–15% of the object's height as a token or a box, not a 1–2 unit offset. Check the largest hero objects first. If any of them shows less side strip than the smallest card vignette, deepen it before you finish.

findings.summary: The subscribe confirmation is a die-cut word badge placed loose on the black footer next to plain text. There is no white ink-framed panel with a static hard shadow, and the badge's ink slab disappears into the black. Compared with the reference's framed, picked-up confirmations, it reads as an inline note rather than a designed moment.
